The autonomous vehicle sector reached a critical commercialization milestone as Uber commenced operations of Europe’s first fully driverless robotaxi service in Croatia, marking the first time such a service operates with zero human safety drivers [Uber started driverless robotaxis in Croatia](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivAFBVV95cUxQQ09uc1FWTGJmNVBER3NyVENJMHVfYWJYcENNdjhsc3dRSkxDejFYdmdOSUFvM1dMNHlCNzVTc0sxZWJzdEdmWmZ1NXZzRmx5aElBR09JZ3U5OURvVFdpVGc1SURETkl1MmwzQ0dmeXV5OUkyQXBZMC03Rl9oYU9kWnN6RHpDOFJFTzVXdW5QbEVSanlMTzBnWnlHaVJFXzhsN1BUbHkteGdJeXJzeU5zNWlLSlVoMkc4NTJLdg?oc=5). This development coincides with Tesla launching its first Cybercab robotaxis in Texas [Tesla launched Cybercabs in Texas](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijwFBVV95cUxNVTdTeWNxeE9xLWkwZGxqQmlCVUQ2T1hOQ2x2WFFtaFNhWmhnWVJZbTQ1MEotWWZXTUh0V3lnX3IwQU5pSERvbnhmRGo3cFJWenFXVU5YT0hrQkR4U1FQN2t6R1FtLVZDY0ZtdERROGlwMWJGTWtZd2prZnRpTmJDalBjdERKWnBjUUs2WnYzUQ?oc=5) and the Texas Department of Transportation confirming that air taxis are taking flight this fall under a new federal program [TxDOT confirmed air taxi flights](https://news.google.?oc=5). These simultaneous launches demonstrate a rapid shift from testing to public revenue-generating operations across multiple continents.

In the defense and security sector, the European Union released $7 billion for Ukraine to purchase Patriot missiles and drones, a move that finally allows Kyiv to place orders for American interceptors [The EU released funds for Ukraine](https://euromaidanpress.com/2026/09/12/the-eu-just-released-7-billion-for-ukraine-to-buy-patriot-missiles-and-drones/). This financial support occurs as Russian drone strikes hit a train near the Polish border, causing international outcry and highlighting the vulnerability of transportation infrastructure to geopolitical conflicts [Russian drones struck a train near Poland](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMi-?oc=5). Concurrently, AeroVironment landed the first-ever production contract for directed-energy weapons in U.S. military history, signaling a strategic pivot toward cost-effective counter-drone technologies [AeroVironment secured a directed-energy contract](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/11/aerovironment-ceo-10-per-shot-laser-beats-150000-drones-but-stock-keeps-falling/).

Regulatory and operational frameworks are also evolving to accommodate these new technologies. The Irish Aviation Authority successfully prosecuted a drone pilot for infringing on restricted airspace, establishing a legal precedent for enforcement [The IAA prosecuted a drone pilot](https://www.suasnews.com/2026/09/iaa-successfully-prosecutes-drone-pilot-for-infringing-on-restricted-airspace/). Meanwhile, Skyworx Drone Shows asked the Federal Communications Commission to exclude purpose-built aerial entertainment drones from proposed restrictions, arguing that current rules could put America’s aerial light shows at risk [Skyworx asked the FCC for an exclusion](https://dronedj.com/2026/09/14/skyworx-swarming-drone-fcc-ban/).
